title: Day 6 Progress of my Spore like, and What Stopped it from going off the rails already
author: Diligent_Historian93
selftext:
So I used to spend hours playing in the creature demo of Spore when I was young, because I come from a third world country and we had one shitty computer and no money for games. The Spore Demo was free and I used to just love making a 1000 different creatures and watching them come to life. 

With Opus 5.5 and all the games' showcase people were doing, I thought to myself ay, why cant I make what I wanted to play myself? And started experimenting with it. I was able to make procedural animation for the creatures, clay like body that shapes and molds itself, and now a fully functioning creature editor, and I just feel like a kid again.

There were many hitches along the 6 day ride already haha. The biggest one was opus' tendency to tunnel vision. Since you can make your own creatures in my game, the possibilities are endless, and getting everything to work for every creature seamlessly is not easy, especially with procedural animation. I was trying to implement creatures bending down to drink water, and the Opus instance spent like 3 hours drilling down, testing it against every creature in my 500 creature test set, overfitting to specific creature bodies.

I had to stop it and bring it back, and get it to look at the big picture again, and the thing that helped it reset was my guidelines.

The first day I spent completely on just making a comprehensive design doc for the whole game, implementation specifics, marketing specifics, game loop specifics, and to the cornerstone of my whole project is the motto "The players make what they want, it looks and feels exactly like they want it to". 

The first time this guiding principle helped was when we were implementing the creature editor itself. There are some designs, like this one, which don't have a balance point and shouldn't work, but I want to let players create what they want. So instead of invalidating that design in the editor, we just show the balance point, tell the players its wonky and let them make it still, and it supports itself with its legs even though it shouldn't.

Then the big one, leaning down to drink water. As you can expect with the varied bodies, it was a task, and opus went tasking. After i noticed it making like 10 revisions for a single body I asked it to pull back. For one of the bodies there was no graceful way to get it to bend, so I told Opus to just let it flop to the floor and drink water that way. And I also asked it why it couldn't come up with the solution itself instead of overfitting. Instead it was trying to get the body to bend in weird ways which would ruin that specific body's fantasy. We clearly mention in the docs to do extensive research before steps and to make graceful fallbacks if the design can't do a certain task, whether that be flopping down to drink water, or just tell the player that they can design this body, but it wont be able to do X.

The reasoning according to Opus was that when it has pre conceived notions, like the work of a different agent that it inherits, it can tunnel vision into making it work, so to say. It didn't give enough priority to the docs. Now every new instance gets a big fat line saying the design doc is god.

Since that little mishap its been great. Now my Kins can eat, sleep, roar, call for help, freeze when alerted, have idle animations and many such little actions, all procedurally generated. They feel alive now. And after that water debacle, I never had to correct opus from tunnel visioning or overfitting again because the guideline is crystal clear.

If you'd like to playtest or help me in development or guide development, feel free to join my discord: QQbUkDAn6N

**TLDR: BEFORE YOU START MAKING A GAME, THINK ABOUT WHAT THE PLAYERS' JOURNEY SHOULD LOOK LIKE, WHATS THE GAMEPLAY LOOP, WHATS THE FANTASY, WHATS ACCEPTABLE AND WHATS NOT ACCEPTABLE. SPEND A CONSIDERATE AMOUNT OF TIME ON MAKING A DOCUMENT ABOUT THESE THINGS AND MAKING SURE ALL YOUR AGENTS FOLLOW IT. MIGHT SEEM OBVIOUS, BUT I KNOW A LOT OF PEOPLE ARE TRYING THINGS AND MIGHT NOT KNOW THIS.**
